newsitem.title: PERU: Peru doubles security at siege site after arrests.
newsitem.headline: Peru doubles security at siege site after arrests.

text.p: Peru doubled its security around the besieged Japanese ambassador's residence on Saturday following the arrest of three guerrilla suspects at the site the day before, officials said.
Heavily-armed Marxist guerrillas were holding 103 VIP hostages at the residence and have mined its grounds.
"We have doubled the number of officers -- especially in the intelligence and criminal units -- to avoid surprises," the head of the country's special tactics police, Juan Carlos Mejia, said.

The security forces increased to 300 their uniformed police officers and sent an additional 50 plainclothes intelligence officers to the middle-class San Isidro ditrict, where scores of journalists were camping out, Mejia said.

Two women and one man, all claiming to be street sellers, were arrested on Friday after police found false identity papers, together with maps and plans, in their bags, according to an anti-terrorist police source.
